stimuli.text: Researchers want to investigate whether a new phone app reduces evening screen time. They have 60 volunteer students available.

Random samples of 15 were taken from two groups. The values of reaction time (hundredths of a second) are:

**Morning:** 10, 12, 16, 18, 19, 20, 20, 20, 22, 22, 23, 25, 25, 28, 29

**Evening:** 16, 18, 18, 19, 21, 22, 28, 32, 35, 38, 39, 41, 42, 43, 62
A school district claims that 30% of its students take public transit to school. A reporter suspects the true proportion is lower. In a random sample of 180 students, 40 take public transit.

Data were collected on age of car (years) (x) and price (thousands of dollars) (y) for a sample of used cars. A scatterplot shows a linear pattern, and the residual plot shows no pattern. Computer output for the least-squares regression is shown.

```text
Predictor   Coef      SE Coef
Constant    59.9
x           -1.6
S = 4.9    R-Sq = 56.0%
```

questions.stem: Which change increases the power of a significance test, with everything else unchanged?

options.text: Using a two-sided instead of a one-sided test
options.why: For the correct direction, that lowers power.
That lowers power.
Correct. Larger samples detect real effects more often.
That lowers power.

questions.explanation: Larger samples detect real effects more often.

questions.stem: Each of 7 independent devices fails with probability 0.1. What is the probability that at least one fails?

options.why: That is the probability none fail.
Correct. 1 − P(none fail) = 1 − (1 − p)^n.
Probabilities of overlapping events cannot simply be added.
That is the probability all fail.

questions.stem: The correlation between hours studied and exam score is r = 0.95. Which is a correct interpretation of r²?

options.text: Hours studied causes 90.3% of exam score
options.why: Regression does not establish causation.

options.text: About 95% of the variation in exam score is accounted for by the model
options.why: Square r.

options.text: About 90.3% of the predictions are correct
options.why: r² is about variation explained, not accuracy of individual predictions.

options.text: About 90.3% of the variation in exam score is accounted for by the linear model relating exam score to hours studied
options.why: Correct. r² is the proportion of variation in y explained by the linear model.

questions.stem: Which graph is appropriate for displaying the distribution of favorite music genres among students?

options.why: Scatterplots need two quantitative variables.
Histograms are for quantitative data.

questions.stem: A variable is approximately normal with mean 59 and standard deviation 4. What value is at the 25th percentile?

options.why: Use the z-score for the percentile, not the percentile itself.
Correct. z = invNorm(0.25) ≈ -0.674; x = μ + zσ.
Check the sign of z.
Multiply z by σ, not σ².

questions.stem: A 95% confidence interval for μ₁ − μ₂ is (−2.4, 5.1). What can be concluded?

options.text: There is no convincing evidence of a difference in population means, because 0 is in the interval
options.why: Correct. Zero is a plausible difference.
Negative differences are also plausible.

options.text: The two means are exactly equal
options.why: The interval does not prove equality.
Positive differences are also plausible.

questions.stem: A residual plot shows a clear curved pattern. What does this indicate?

options.text: A linear model is not appropriate for the data
options.why: Correct. Curvature in residuals means the relationship is not linear.
A good fit shows no pattern.
Not necessarily.
Unrelated.

questions.explanation: Curvature in residuals means the relationship is not linear.

questions.stem: The data are: 10, 13, 13, 18, 25, 32, 34, 39, 72. Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, which statement is correct?

options.text: Q1 = 13, Q3 = 36.5; values above 71.8 are outliers, so 72 is an outlier
options.why: Correct. IQR = 23.5; upper fence = Q3 + 1.5·IQR = 71.8.

options.text: Q1 = 13, Q3 = 36.5; values above 60.3 are outliers
options.why: Add 1.5·IQR to Q3, not to the median.

options.text: There are no outliers because every value is within 2 standard deviations of the mean
options.why: The 1.5 × IQR rule is the method asked for.

options.text: Q1 = 13, Q3 = 36.5; values above 60 are outliers, so 72 is an outlier
options.why: The fence uses 1.5 × IQR, not 1 × IQR.

questions.stem: A student is chosen at random from those who drive to school. What is the probability the student is a junior?

options.why: That is P(junior) overall.
Correct. P(junior | drives) = juniors who drive ÷ all who drive.
That is P(drives | junior).
That is P(junior and drives); divide by drivers only.

questions.stem: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A and B) = 0.15. What is P(A or B), and are A and B independent?

options.why: Subtract P(A and B) so the overlap is not counted twice.
Compare P(A and B) with P(A)·P(B) = 0.15.
Correct. P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); independent if P(A and B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.15.
P(A and B) is not 0, so they are not mutually exclusive.

questions.stem: For a distribution of number of social media followers, the mean is 43 and the median is 56. Which is the most likely shape?

options.why: Correct. A long left tail pulls the mean below the median.
The mean is pulled toward the tail.
A uniform distribution is symmetric, with mean near the median.
In a symmetric distribution, the mean and median are close.

questions.explanation: Mean 43 < median 56: the mean is pulled toward the left tail.

questions.stem: Which variable is quantitative?

options.why: That is categorical.
Zip codes are labels.

questions.stem: Two independent random samples have n₁ = 34, s₁ = 8 and n₂ = 51, s₂ = 4. What is the standard error of x̄₁ − x̄₂?

options.why: Each sample contributes s²/n.
Add variances, then take the square root; standard errors do not add.
Correct. √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂).
Variances add, even for a difference.

questions.stem: In a random sample of 280 customers of an online store, 81 would recommend it to a friend. Which is a 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all customers of an online store who would recommend it to a friend?

options.why: Correct. p̂ ± z*√(p̂(1 − p̂)/n) with z* = 1.96.
Use the standard error, √(p̂(1 − p̂)/n).
Divide by n inside the square root.
Multiply the standard error by z*.

questions.stem: Which statistic is an unbiased estimator of the population proportion?

options.text: The median of the sample values
options.why: Not an estimator of a proportion.

options.text: The proportion from a voluntary response sample
options.why: Voluntary response is biased.

options.text: The largest proportion among several samples
options.why: That would tend to overestimate.

options.text: The sample proportion p̂ from a random sample
options.why: Correct. Its sampling distribution is centered at p.

questions.explanation: Its sampling distribution is centered at p.

questions.stem: Does increasing the sample size reduce bias in a survey?

options.why: Size never fixes bias.

parts.prompt: Write an investigative question for this study, and identify the explanatory and response variables.

rubric.criterion: A clear investigative question that names the population or units and the variables.
rubric.example: "Does the app lead to a better average evening screen time over two weeks than no app for units like these?"
Explanatory: treatment (the app vs no app). Response: average evening screen time over two weeks.

parts.prompt: Explain why an experiment, rather than an observational study, should be used to answer the question.

rubric.criterion: Only random assignment allows a cause-and-effect conclusion; an observational study could be confounded.
rubric.example: Units that choose a treatment may differ in other ways that affect the response.

parts.prompt: Describe how to randomly assign the 60 units to the two treatments in a completely randomized design.

rubric.example: Number units 1–60; use a random number generator to select 30 different numbers.
Those 30 receive the app; the remaining 30 receive no app.

parts.prompt: The researchers consider blocking by grade level (9th and 12th graders use phones differently). Explain how blocking would be carried out and why it could improve the experiment.

rubric.criterion: Form blocks and randomize within each block.
rubric.example: Separate units into the blocks, then randomly assign half of each block to each treatment.

rubric.criterion: Benefit: reduces variability in the response due to the blocking variable, making a treatment effect easier to detect.
rubric.example: Accounts for differences caused by grade level.

parts.prompt: Find the five-number summary for each group.
Use the 1.5 × IQR rule to determine whether Evening has any outliers. Show your work.

rubric.example: IQR = 22; upper fence = 41 + 1.5(22) = 74. No outliers.

parts.prompt: Compare the distributions of the two groups (shape, center and variability) in context.

rubric.example: The median for Evening (32) is greater than for Morning (20).
Evening is more variable (IQR 22 vs 7).

rubric.criterion: Comments on shape or unusual features.
rubric.example: Describes the shapes using the summaries.

parts.prompt: Which measure of center is more appropriate for Evening, the mean or the median? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Median, because it is resistant to the outlier or skew.
rubric.example: Mean 31.6 is pulled toward the high value; median 32 is not.

parts.prompt: State the hypotheses, defining the parameter.

rubric.criterion: Correct hypotheses with the parameter defined.
rubric.example: H₀: p = 0.3; Hₐ: p < 0.3, where p is the proportion of all district students who take public transit.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure and check its conditions.

rubric.criterion: One-sample z test for a proportion.
rubric.example: Random sample stated.
180 is less than 10% of all students (assumed); np₀ = 54 and n(1 − p₀) = 126 are both at least 10.

parts.prompt: Calculate the test statistic and p-value.
State a conclusion in context at α = 0.05.

rubric.criterion: Correct decision linked to the p-value, in context.
rubric.example: Because 0.0114 is less than 0.05, reject H₀: convincing evidence that the proportion is less than 0.3.

parts.prompt: Write the equation of the least-squares regression line, defining the variables.

rubric.example: ŷ = 59.9 − 1.6x, where ŷ is predicted price (thousands of dollars) and x is age of car (years).

parts.prompt: Interpret the slope and the value of R-Sq in context.

rubric.example: For each additional unit of age of car (years), the predicted price (thousands of dollars) decreases by about 1.6.
About 56.0% of the variation in price (thousands of dollars) is accounted for by the linear model with age of car (years).

parts.prompt: One observation has x = 9 and y = 41.6. Calculate and interpret its residual. Also find the correlation r.

rubric.example: ŷ = 45.5; residual = 41.6 − 45.5 = -3.9: the actual value is below the prediction.

parts.prompt: The data come from a convenience sample. Explain how this affects the conclusions and describe a better data collection method.

rubric.criterion: Results may not generalize to the population; a random sample would allow generalization.
rubric.example: Take a simple random sample of used cars from the population of interest. Observational data also cannot show causation.
